question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in global `tools.exec.pty` default for shell exec, and what guardrails should apply around sandbox and approval-backed execution?
rationale: The code change is small, but the setting changes default shell-exec runtime mode and intersects the project’s high bar for config/security surfaces, so automation should not choose the product/security tradeoff alone.

options.title: Approve Narrow Opt-In Config
options.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` as an explicit opt-in default with per-call override, full direct/gateway coverage, sandbox diagnostics, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep PTY Per Call Only
options.body: Decline the global config surface and document that trusted workflows must request PTY per command or through skill guidance.

options.title: Defer Until Sandbox PTY Policy Lands
options.body: Resolve the sandbox warning/error policy first, then revisit whether a global PTY default is safe enough to expose.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Opt-In Config
recommendation.body: Add `tools.exec.pty` as an explicit opt-in default with per-call override, full direct/gateway coverage, sandbox diagnostics, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle authored the original PTY support and fallback behavior and is the strongest history signal for the exec-mode boundary decision.
